description: Issue #867: neutralizes RequestBindingPolicy.IsPathAllowed's declaring-type/gateway-name guard (`if (IsBannedGatewayMember(member)) return false;`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs) with a compile-preserving `&& false` (not a deletion), reproducing the pre-fix state where BaseController.RedoUpdateModel/BaseApiController.RedoUpdateModel wrote every caller-supplied form/query key onto a VM with zero restriction. The static-member guard on the preceding line stays intact, so this mutant isolates the gateway/declaring-type check specifically. Checked against two independent HTTP-level tests in RequestBindingScopeHttpTests867: GetPagingData_HostileConfigInfoIsQuickDebugField_DoesNotFlipConfig_LegitimateSearcherBindingStillWorks (direct key 'ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug') and GetPagingData_HostileAliasedConfigInfoFields_DoNotFlipConfig (the issue's own alias example, 'Searcher.Wtm.ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug', plus the depth-cap-isolating 'Wtm.ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug'). Both assert on WTMContext's actual process-wide IOptionsMonitor<Configs>.CurrentValue.IsQuickDebug value (resolved from the factory's own DI container, the SAME instance WTMContext.ConfigInfo captures), not a response status code -- with the guard neutralized, the POST still returns 200 (RedoUpdateModel's own catch swallows nothing relevant here) and IsQuickDebug is observably flipped to true, which is what turns both assertions red. The green control, GetPagingData_HostileSearcherModeBatchField_DoesNotBypassRowFiltering, posts only 'Searcher.ZipCode'/'SearcherMode'/'Ids' -- none of which are gateway-banned names -- so it is genuinely unaffected by this mutant, proving the guard's removal does not have broader collateral effects than declared.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.IsPathAllowed(Type, string, string) -- the `if (IsBannedGatewayMember(member)) return false;` guard condition

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.RequestBindingS: a caller-supplied 'ConfigInfo\.IsQuickDebug' form field must never reach the process-wide Configs singleton
neither the 'Wtm\.ConfigInfo\.IsQuickDebug' nor the aliased 'Searcher\.Wtm\.ConfigInfo\.IsQuickDebug' form field may reach the process-wide Configs singleton

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first): GetPagingData_HostileConfigInfoIsQuickDebugField_DoesNotFlipConfig_LegitimateSearcherBindingStillWorks -> 'Assert.IsFalse failed. #867: a caller-supplied '\''ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug'\'' form field must never reach the process-wide Configs singleton through RedoUpdateModel's raw reflection write.'; GetPagingData_HostileAliasedConfigInfoFields_DoNotFlipConfig -> 'Assert.IsFalse failed. #867: neither the '\''Wtm.ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug'\'' nor the aliased '\''Searcher.Wtm.ConfigInfo.IsQuickDebug'\'' form field may reach the process-wide Configs singleton — the declaring-type check must catch '\''Wtm'\'' wherever in the dotted path it appears, not just as the key's literal first segment.'. Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-gateway-declaring-type-guard-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'. (Earlier run surfaced a real test-isolation defect: both red tests share _strictFactory's process-wide IOptionsMonitor<Configs> instance, and the first test's own hostile write -- let through by this exact mutant -- was not being reset, so the second test's baseline sanity check failed first (UNEXPECTED_RED) instead of its own assertion. Fixed by wrapping both tests' bodies in try/finally that resets IsQuickDebug=false regardless of pass/fail, then re-verified KILLED.)
